newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan woman stoned to death for adultery - radio.
newsitem.headline: Afghan woman stoned to death for adultery - radio.

text.p: A woman has been stoned to death in the eastern Afghan province of Laghman after Islamic judges found her guilty of adultery, Afghanistan's official Kabul radio said on Saturday.

The broadcast, monitored in Islamabad, did not give the date of the execution of Jamila, who it said was sentenced after her husband, Aminullah, caught her while trying to flee with a stranger, Abdullah, to another district in Laghman.
Aminullah killed Abdullah and was sentenced to 12 years in jail, said the radio, controlled by the Taleban Islamic movement which rules more than two-thirds of Afghanistan, including Laghman.
"Jamila was stoned to death on the charge of adultery," the radio said. It did not say who did the stoning or whether it was carried out in public.

The Taleban, which captured Kabul last September after ousting president Burhanuddin Rabbani, has enforced strict Islamic laws in areas under its control, including a ban on women going out without wearing an all-embracing Burqa veil and curbs on their right to education and work.
The Taleban is fighting an alliance of forces loyal to Rabbani and Uzbek chief General Abdul Rashid Rashid Dostum.
